# Spec: external-board
<!-- Generated by /hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-10-05 -->

## Overview

Board item HEF-14, requested by fxcube-project (fxcube `tasks/initiatives/lane-setup-v2.md` §4 G1).
Hefesto assumes the board and the code share one repository:
- `session-launch.sh` reads `$TOP/.claude/project-status.json` of the code repo;
- `status-board.sh` resolves `root` against that repo's top;
- the ledger lives in the code repo's git common dir, so "one worker per repository" only ever sees
  one repository.

fxcube's board is its own git repo (`tasks/`), and it feeds three code repos (`operations_api`,
`cube_ui`, `production_server`).

This feature adds an **external board** mode. Unconfigured, it is today's `in-repo` mode exactly.

```jsonc
// <code repo>/.claude/project-status.json — a pointer (plus that repo's own `branches`, HEF-15)
{ "board": "../tasks", "branches": { "integration": "dev" } }

// <board repo>/.claude/project-status.json — the board config as today, plus the repos it feeds
{ "source": "tasks-repo", "root": ".", "orchestrate": { … },
  "repos": { "ops": "../operations_api", "ui": "../cube_ui", "ps": "../production_server" } }
```

Decisions taken here:

- **The pointer lives in the code repo; the map lives in the board.**
  - A code repo names its board with `board` (a path relative to its top, or absolute).
  - The board names the repos it feeds with `repos` (name → path relative to the board's top).
  - Running from the board repo itself works too: its config has `repos`, so it is the board.
- **Which config holds what:**
  - The board config holds the board fields, `orchestrate` (tiers, caps, allowlists, publish,
    escalate, panes) and `kinds`.
  - Each code repo's own config holds its `branches` (HEF-15), because ops and ui may integrate
    differently.
- **One central ledger** in the board repo's git common dir (`<board>/.git/hefesto/ledger/`). Every
  entry records `repo: <name>`, so ownership, `list`, `metrics` and escalation see every repo the
  board feeds. The ledger stays outside every checkout and is never committed.
- **Item → repo routing:**
  - An item names its repo on a body line `repo: <name>`.
  - An item with no `repo:` line goes to the board's only repo when there is exactly one.
  - Otherwise it is refused with "names no repo (add `repo: <name>`; the board feeds: ops, ui, ps)".
  - An item naming two repos (`repo: ops, ui`) is refused with "targets 2 repos (ops, ui) — split it
    into one item per repo".
  - Both refusals happen at registration. The orchestrator reports them and moves on; nothing is
    written to the ledger for that item.
- **One worker per repository, by repo:** `ledger.sh next` skips an entry whose repo already has an
  owned entry. In-repo mode has no `repo` on any entry, so one active entry still blocks dispatch
  everywhere, as today.
- **Where sessions run:** the planner, the worker, the verifier and the deploy babysitter run in the
  entry's repo (`<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<id>`). The launcher can be started from the board repo or
  from any code repo the board feeds.
- **Board writes land in the board repo:** `publish`'s `--mark` edits the board file there, and the
  person commits it. Committing automatically (`publish_commit`) is deferred to board item HEF-16,
  which records the guards it needs.

## User Scenarios

### US1: Reading an external board from a code repo [P1]
- **Given** `operations_api/.claude/project-status.json` = `{"board": "../tasks"}` and the board config with `repos`
- **When** `status-board.sh` (or `/hef.status`) runs in `operations_api`
- **Then** it prints the board from `../tasks`, and `--item`, `--item-raw`, `--item-kind` read items from there
- **Edge**: run from inside `../tasks` itself → the same output (the board repo is its own board)
- **Error**: `board` points at a path with no board config → it dies naming the path

### US2: Routing an item to its repo [P1]
- **Given** an item `## OPS-12 — …` whose body has `repo: ops`
- **When** `status-board.sh --item-repo OPS-12` runs
- **Then** it prints `ops` and the absolute path of `../operations_api`, tab-separated
- **Edge**: no `repo:` line and exactly one repo declared → that repo
- **Error**: `repo: ops, ui` → "targets 2 repos (ops, ui) — split it"; `repo: web` (undeclared) → "names repo 'web' the board does not feed (ops, ui, ps)"

### US3: Dispatching from one repo into another [P1]
- **Given** an external board whose next item targets `ui`
- **When** `/hef.orchestrate --dry-run` runs in `operations_api`
- **Then**:
  - registration records `repo: ui` on the central ledger entry;
  - `session-launch.sh implement <id> --dry-run` prints a line whose worktree is `cube_ui/.claude/worktrees/<id>`;
  - the tiers and allowlist come from the board's `orchestrate` block;
  - the PR base and the verifier's diff base come from `cube_ui`'s own `branches`.

### US4: One worker per repo, several repos at once [P1]
- **Given** an owned entry for `ops` and a queued entry for `ui`
- **When** `ledger.sh next --stage build` runs
- **Then** it returns the `ui` entry
- **And** a second queued `ops` entry is skipped until the first is released

### US5: Hand-run, publish and status against the external board [P2]
- **Given** an external board
- **When** someone runs `ledger.sh handoff <id> --pr <url>` from a code repo branch
- **Then** the central entry records that repo (resolved by matching the current repo's path against `repos`)
- **And** `ledger.sh publish <id>` marks the heading in the board repo's file (the person commits it)
- **And** `/hef.status` shows the external board and the ledger's AI-delivery numbers

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | **Board resolution, one owner.** `ledger.sh board` prints `{mode, board_top, config, ledger_dir, repos, repo}` as JSON, where `repo` is the current repo's name in external mode and null otherwise.<br>- `in-repo`: the current repo's config, today's ledger dir, `repos` null.<br>- `external`: from a code repo's `board` pointer, or from a config that has `repos` itself.<br>It dies naming the field for: a `board` path with no config; `repos` that is not an object of name → path; a repo path that does not exist; a name outside `[a-z0-9_-]+`. Every script asks `ledger.sh board` instead of re-deriving it. | P1 | US1, US3 |
| FR-002 | `status-board.sh` reads the resolved board. The config and `root` come from `board_top` (`--config` still wins). The new `--item-repo <id>` prints `<name>\t<abs path>`, or refuses as in US2. | P1 | US1, US2 |
| FR-003 | `ledger.sh` writes the central ledger in external mode. `init … --repo <name>` records `.repo` (validated against `repos`; required in external mode, refused in in-repo mode). On an external board, `next` enforces one worker per repo: it skips any entry whose `.repo` has an owned entry, refuses an entry with no `.repo`, and names each busy repo and its owner when nothing is left. In-repo, `next` is unchanged and the one-worker rule stays in `/hef.orchestrate` step 2, as before. `list`, `metrics`, `escalate` and `publish` read the central ledger. | P1 | US3, US4 |
| FR-004 | `session-launch.sh` resolves the entry's repo:<br>- in external mode, `TOP` = the entry's repo path (worktrees, cwd, `branches`);<br>- the orchestrate block (tiers, caps, allowlists) comes from the board config;<br>- the ledger is the central one.<br>In in-repo mode nothing changes. | P1 | US3 |
| FR-005 | `/hef.orchestrate` step 1 registers with `--repo "$(status-board.sh --item-repo <id> \| cut -f1)"` in external mode. A routing refusal is reported and the item is skipped, with no ledger write. Step 2 reports the owned entries, and step 3's `next` enforces one worker per repo. | P1 | US3, US4 |
| FR-006 | `ledger.sh handoff` in external mode records the current repo (matched by path against `repos`; a repo the board does not feed is refused). `publish` marks the board file in the board repo; committing it stays the person's (auto-commit deferred to HEF-16). | P2 | US5 |
| FR-007 | Docs: `docs/install.md` §7 step 13 (external board), README §5, `docs/hooks.md` (`board`, `--item-repo`, `--repo`), `docs/architecture.md`, CHANGELOG; board HEF-14 → DOING. | P2 | all |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | `ledger.sh board`: in-repo defaults; external mode from a code repo and from the board repo; each refusal named | `tests/smoke.sh` |
| SC-002 | A fixture with a board repo and two code repos (ops: `integration: dev`; ui: trunk):<br>- `status-board` from ops shows the board, and the item commands read it;<br>- `--item-repo` routes and refuses (two repos, undeclared, none with several repos);<br>- `init --repo` writes the central ledger;<br>- `next` skips an owned repo and returns another;<br>- the implement dry run from ops for a ui item targets ui's worktree with no `--base`, and an ops item targets `--base dev`;<br>- `handoff` from an ops branch records `ops`;<br>- `publish` marks the board file in the board repo, not the code repo;<br>- an unconfigured single repo behaves exactly as before. | `tests/smoke.sh` |
| SC-003 | Mutations: the pointer ignored, the central ledger dir, the per-repo `next` filter, the two-repo refusal, the launcher's repo `TOP`, the main-worktree resolution, `--configured` reading `repo_config`, the unblock `cd`, comment-stripped routing, and the empty `--repo` refusal. Each turns the suite red. | `tests/smoke.sh` |
| SC-004 | fxcube acceptance: from `operations_api`, `/hef.orchestrate --dry-run` and `session-launch.sh implement <id> --dry-run` read `../tasks`, target the item's repo, and base on `dev`. Prerequisite: the dispatched items carry `repo:` lines (none do today), the pointer and `repos` map are in place, and ops's `branches` declares `dev` | user-run |

## Clarifications
_None. Worker environment isolation (`worker_setup`, per-worker env vars) is lower priority in the request and is left for a follow-up item._
